topic: Using std::ostream_iterator for Output Stream Iteration
explanation: In modern C++, std::ostream_iterator is a template class that facilitates outputting elements to an output stream (such as std::cout or file streams) using iterator semantics. It allows algorithms to write directly to streams in a clean, generic way, enabling seamless integration with the Standard Template Library (STL) algorithms. This approach promotes a functional programming style and simplifies code that involves outputting sequences of data.
code_example: // Create an ostream_iterator for integers with a comma and space as delimiter
// Use std::copy to output the vector elements to std::cout
example_explanation: This example demonstrates creating an std::ostream_iterator for integers that outputs to std::cout, separated by commas. Using std::copy, it writes each element of the vector 'numbers' directly to the output stream via the iterator. This showcases how std::ostream_iterator enables seamless, iterator-based output of sequences, integrating with STL algorithms for concise and expressive code in modern C++.
